narrative.overview:
Plainsong is a calm, warm, unhurried room you come back to for the things you set aside. Warm paper, charcoal ink and a single blue-black accent. Nothing in it competes for attention, because the tabs that were closed were already competing too much. The notebook is where a summary is read, not where the interface shows off.

Two type voices split the work. Newsreader, a reading serif, carries everything that was *kept*: titles, TL;DRs, takeaways and the article itself. IBM Plex Sans carries everything you *do*: navigation, buttons, filters and settings. IBM Plex Mono marks *data*: domains, timestamps and counts. All three are bundled locally, so the extension makes no font requests.

Density follows the surface. In the side panel it is compact (13px body, one column, filters in a drawer). In a full tab it opens up (14px body, a persistent sidebar and a card grid). Both are one page with one stylesheet.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white paper and charcoal text. Never pure white or pure black.
One accent, ink blue, used for links, the active nav item, focus and the primary button.
Serif for content, sans for controls, mono for data.
Flat surfaces separated by hairline rules. Shadows only on things that float.
Status shown by a muted hue plus a word, never by colour alone.
A full dark scheme through `prefers-color-scheme`, with every token redefined.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink blue is the only accent. Moss, ochre and brick appear only as status, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Archived Is Quiet Rule
rules.body: Archived is the default state, so its badge has no hue (paper-muted fill, secondary text). Colour is reserved for states that need attention.

rules.name: The Fixed Toast Rule
rules.body: Toasts use their own fixed-colour tokens in both schemes, so the contrast of the Undo button never depends on page tokens.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif means content, sans means controls, mono means data. A new element picks its font by what it *is*, not by how it should look.

rules.name: The No Faux Bold Rule
rules.body: Only the bundled weights exist: Newsreader 400, 400 italic and 600; Plex Sans 400 and 600; Plex Mono 400. Emphasis in mono comes from colour, not weight.

rules.name: The Only Floating Things Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: If an element sits in the page flow, it gets a rule, not a shadow.

dos: **Do** take every colour from the tokens on `:root` and define its dark counterpart under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`.
**Do** set content in Newsreader, controls in Plex Sans and data in Plex Mono (the Three Voices Rule).
**Do** separate surfaces with 1px rules and tonal steps. Reserve shadows for menus, dialogs and toasts.
**Do** pair every status hue with a word and an icon, and keep Archived neutral.
**Do** keep filled ink buttons at `night-ink-fill` in dark mode, not the bright `night-ink`.
**Do** keep a visible focus halo and AA contrast in both schemes, and respect reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent colour, or use moss, ochre or brick decoratively.
**Don't** use pure white (#FFFFFF) or pure black (#000000) surfaces.
**Don't** put shadows on resting cards, inputs or the sidebar.
**Don't** use font weights that aren't bundled, or load fonts from a CDN.

**Don't** fork the token names between pages: `src/options/options.css` currently uses `--bg-page`, `--bg-card` and `--text-main` for the same values that `src/app/app.css` calls `--bg-primary`, `--bg-surface` and `--text-primary`.
